Header**Include the company logo, Services, Our Work, Pricing, About, Resources, and a prominent Contact Us button. Make the navigation responsive and functional.**2. Hero Section**Create a bold headline explaining how the agency helps businesses grow through digital products and technology.Add a short supporting paragraph, a primary “Start a Project” button, and a secondary “View Our Work” button. Use an attractive product interface mockup or carefully designed visual on the right.**3. Trust Section**Create a clean area for client logos and credibility indicators. Selected Projects**Display projects in premium cards with screenshots or interface mockups, project names, short descriptions, services provided, and case-study links. Results and Benefits**Explain how the agency helps clients launch products, improve user experience, simplify operations, and grow their businesses. Do not fabricate performance statistics.**7. Why Choose Us**Show the agency's strengths, development process, communication standards, and support options.**8. Pricing**Create an elegant pricing section with editable service packages. Contact Section**Create a compelling call to action and a working project inquiry form with name, email, company, service type, budget range, and project description fields. FAQ and Footer**Add an interactive FAQ accordion, company information, navigation links, social links, contact details, and privacy and terms links.### Technical Requirements1. Inspect the existing project and its framework before making changes.2. Reuse the existing stack when practical. For a new project, use Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.3. Build reusable components and maintain a clean project structure.4. Implement real navigation and functional interactive elements.5. Add appropriate responsive layouts, accessibility features, and SEO metadata.6. Optimize images and performance.7. Do not create fake backend integrations. Clearly identify any required API credentials or backend setup.8. Use English for all visible website content, including navigation, headings, buttons, forms, messages, and footer text.9. Do not stop after creating a static mockup. Implement the website, run the available checks, fix errors, and verify that the main interactions work.Start by inspecting the project, then build the complete website. Prioritize exceptional design quality, consistent styling, and working functionality.

content.text:
I built the full site as **Halden Digital**, a placeholder brand I invented. It's a Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind 4 project in `/app`, running now at https://preview-16d48385a836fcaa.up.railway.app. The public URL only answers from your own IP until you claim the VM.

`tsc` and `next build` pass. In the browser I checked that clicking a service pre-fills the form, the validation messages appear, and the FAQ accordion opens. I also checked that the mobile menu opens and that there is no horizontal overflow at 390px.

The contact form can't deliver messages yet. A submission today shows "Our inquiry form isn't connected yet", because the email provider isn't set up. To turn it on, create a Resend account and set `RESEND_API_KEY`, `CONTACT_TO_EMAIL` and `CONTACT_FROM_EMAIL` (see `.env.example`). I haven't tested actual email delivery. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to your real domain too.

**Design**
- **Look:** white and light-gray backgrounds with black text and a signal-orange accent (`#ff4a1c`).
- **Type:** Space Grotesk headlines, Inter body text.
- **Mockups:** all interface mockups are built in code, so there are no image files to load.
- **Motion:** scroll-reveal animations and hover effects, switched off for users who prefer reduced motion.

**Content, all in English and in your 10-section order**
- **Header:** sticky, with a working mobile menu and a Contact Us button.
- **Hero:** headline, supporting paragraph, Start a Project and View Our Work buttons, and a dashboard mockup on the right.
- **Trust:** logo and statistic placeholders that are clearly labelled, with no invented clients or numbers.
- **Selected projects:** four cards marked "Concept". Their case-study links lead to the contact form, because no real case studies exist yet.
- **Services:** all nine, each with an icon and an Enquire action that pre-selects that service in the form.
- **Results and benefits, Why choose us, Pricing, FAQ:** built as specified. Pricing shows "Request a Quote" on every package.
- **Contact:** the form has the six fields you listed, plus validation, a loading state, a success message and error messages.
- **Footer:** company info, navigation, social links, contact details, and privacy and terms links.

**Other additions**
- **Spam protection:** the form has a hidden honeypot field.
- **Search and SEO:** metadata, Open Graph tags, `robots.txt`, a sitemap, structured data and a favicon.
- **Accessibility:** a skip link and focus styles.

**To fill in before launch**
- Edit `src/content/site.ts` for your contact details, social links, services, packages, prices and FAQs. The email, phone and address in it are placeholders.
- The Privacy and Terms pages are template placeholders and need real text reviewed by a legal professional.

To run it, use `npm run dev` for development. For production, run `npm run build` and then `npm start`. I haven't deployed it to Railway or pushed it to a repo. I can do either if you want.

Сайт одоо бүхэлдээ монгол кирилл бичгээр байна. Шинэ эффектүүд нэмэгдсэн бөгөөд https://preview-16d48385a836fcaa.up.railway.app дээр ажиллаж байна. Production build амжилттай болсон. Хөтөч дээр нүүр хуудас болон үйлчилгээний хэсгийг шалгасан. Шинэ хэсгүүд, холбоо барих маягт, мобайл харагдац болон эффектүүдийг нэг бүрчлэн шалгаагүй.

**Фонт**
- Гарчигт Unbounded, үндсэн текстэд Manrope ашигласан.
- Хоёулаа кирилл дэмждэг. Ө, Ү үсэг хөтөч дээр зөв харагдсан.

**Текст**
- Бүх харагдах текст монголоор бичигдсэн. Үүнд цэс, хэсгийн гарчиг, товч, маягтын талбар ба алдааны мэдээлэл, FAQ, футер, нууцлал/нөхцөлийн хуудас, серверийн хариу багтана.
- "Халдэн Дижитал" гэдэг нэр, лого кирилл болсон.
- Шинээр нэмсэн текст:
  - итгэл үзлийн хэсэг
  - дөрвөн зарчим
  - hero дахь нэмэлт өгүүлбэр
  - нэмэлт 2 FAQ
  - илүү дэлгэрэнгүй тайлбарууд
- Багцын тайлбарт бодит үнэ оруулах бол энэ загвараар бичнэ: `"4.9 сая ₮"`.

**Шинэ эффектүүд**
- Hero гарчиг үгээрээ дээш гарч ирнэ. "дижитал бүтээгдэхүүнийг" гэсэн хэсэг гялтганаж гэрэлтэнэ.
- Хуудасны дээд талд гүйлгэсэн хэмжээг харуулах зураас байна.
- Том ✦ тэмдэгтэй, зарим үг нь зөвхөн контуртай гүйдэг текст бүс нэмсэн.
- Гүйлгэх тусам итгэл үзлийн текстийн үгс нэг нэгээрээ тод болно.
- Үйлчилгээний картууд курсорыг дагасан улбар шар гэрэлтэй.
- Төслийн картууд хулганы хөдөлгөөнөөр 3D-ээр бага зэрэг хазайна.

Эхлээд "English-only" гэж хүссэн байсан тул үүнийг таны шинэ хүсэлтээр сольсон. Имэйл хаяг, URL зэрэг техникийн утгууд латин хэвээр үлдсэн.

content.thinking:
I'm planning an admin panel at /admin, password-protected via an environment variable, storing all editable content in a JSON file on disk — noting that Railway's disk is ephemeral unless a volume is attached. I need to map out everything that should become editable: site nav, ticker, manifesto, services, projects, benefits, strengths, steps, principles, packages, FAQs, budgets, and various hardcoded heading text currently baked into components.

To make truly everything editable, the simplest path is a generic recursive JSON editor that renders inputs for strings, add/remove/reorder controls for arrays, and nested forms for objects — avoiding bespoke forms per content type. I'll need to move the hardcoded copy (hero text, section heads, trust/contact text, footer, UI labels) into the content object itself.

For architecture, I'm setting up default content in a defaults file, a store module that reads and deep-merges saved content over those defaults, and dynamic pages that fetch content server-side and pass it down as props instead of components importing content directly — which means refactoring several components, including client-side ones like the header.

I also need props flowing into the Contact client form for services/budgets, and an auth layer: an ADMIN_PASSWORD env var, HMAC-signed session cookies, login/logout API routes, and a content GET/PUT API with validation and atomic file writes plus a reset-to-defaults option. For the admin UI itself, I'm planning a tabbed interface per content section using the recursive editor, and I'm also considering storing contact form submissions locally in an inquiries file so the admin panel has something useful to show even without email configured.

For pricing, I'm defining four plans in Mongolian: Эхлэл at 400,000₮, Стандарт at 800,000₮, Про/Бизнес at 1,500,000₮, and a custom "Тусгай" tier with no fixed price. I'm adding a priceNote field so plans can show something like "-аас эхэлнэ" (starting from), while the custom plan just displays "Тусгай" with a note like "Үнийн санал авна" and a button prompting users to request a quote.

Each package card will have editable fields — name, price, priceNote, blurb, feature list, featured flag, service, and CTA label — with the recursive editor treating booleans as checkboxes, and the grid laid out as four columns on larger screens collapsing to two on medium.

Now I'm restructuring the content defaults file to hold all site copy and config as a typed object, with sections for site info, navigation, ticker, manifesto, and copy blocks like the hero section's badge, title lines, paragraphs, and CTAs, splitting hero title lines into separate strings by word.

For the rest of the sections I'm mapping out copy groups for work, services, results, about, pricing, and FAQ with their eyebrow/title/text pattern, plus contact fields including an accent title and form-related labels. I've decided to include form labels and success messages in the content object while leaving client-side validation error strings in code, and I'm adding footer copy with nav, social, and contact column titles.

Now I'm covering trust stats, marquee ticker text, manifesto principles, the "howWeWork" section, header nav labels, and legal page content for privacy/terms, while deciding to leave decorative mockup text and aria labels in code. With the structure settled, I'm ready to start writing the actual file by adapting the existing site.ts into a new defaults file that includes all this copy.

I'm keeping individual exports and adding a `copy` object, then assembling a `defaults` bundle from them. For typed fields like service keys, I plan to make the editor treat "key" and "kind" fields as readonly so admins can't break references, while merging saved content over defaults with a deep merge that handles objects key-wise and arrays separately.

Now I'm designing the generic recursive editor: it'll hold the whole content object in state with immutable path-based updates, support array add/remove/reorder controls, use an English label dictionary with fallback to raw key names, and auto-switch to textareas for long or multiline text. Tabs will use top-level keys as English tab names, and I'm setting up a configurable data directory (env var or cwd/data) while adding it to .gitignore.

Pages will use dynamic rendering so file reads happen fresh each request, with metadata and sitemap/robots pulled from content where possible but site URL staying in env config. No image upload needed for this scope. Now I'll start coding — defaults, the file store, and auth first.
